control.name: CONTROL — re-introduce a `gh` exec: a helper that shells the GitHub CLI to release a dispatch claim, exactly the passthrough the enumerated DeleteRef replaced

mutations.name: stop resolving an argv[0] held in a named constant (`const bin = "gh"; exec.Command(bin)` reads as unresolved instead of an invocation)
mutations.new: if v, ok := consts[a.Name]; false && ok {

mutations.name: stop treating exec.CommandContext as a launch site (every context-carrying shell-out becomes invisible)
stop resolving an ALIASED os/exec import (`import xc "os/exec"` hides every launch in the file)
stop resolving a DOT-imported os/exec (`import . "os/exec"` hides every launch in the file)
disable layer 2 entirely: a forge-CLI literal in ANY position stops being a finding, so every wrapper call (`runCmd("gh", …)`, `g.run("gh", …)`) goes unseen
over-broaden layer 2 in the other direction: a switch case naming a forge CLI becomes an invocation, which is the false positive that gets a ban suppressed rather than fixed
round could-not-check up to clean: an exec site whose argv[0] does not resolve stops being reported at all
mutations.old: add(Finding{File: rel, Line: line, Func: enclosing(stack), Via: via, Kind: KindUnresolved})

mutations.name: stop failing closed on a tree with no shipped Go source (a mis-pointed root would certify anything)
mutations.old: return nil, fmt.Errorf("no shipped Go source found under %s — a scan that reads nothing clears everything", root)

mutations.name: stop detecting STALE permit rows, so a permit outlives the call site it was written for and the ratchet stops counting anything real
stop detecting STALE ledger rows, so a retired indirection keeps its could-not-check entry forever
let a ledger row clear an observed INVOCATION (the could-not-check register silently becomes a second permit list)
drop DeleteRef's ref validation on the GitHub backend — the typed op becomes `gh api -X DELETE <anything>` in a typed coat
mutations.new:
clean := ref
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/repos/%s/%s/git/refs/%s", repo.Owner, repo.Name, clean)

mutations.name: stop refusing a ref component that traverses out of the ref namespace (`heads/../../branches/main/protection` reaches branch protection)
stop refusing URL-significant characters in a ref, so a ref can reshape the request it is interpolated into
let the GitLab backend serve a non-branch ref namespace by pretending the branch delete applies — a still-held claim would be reported released
let a backend export a raw-request escape hatch outside the frozen surface (the passthrough the callsite scan cannot see, which is why the shape check exists)
